paper: FinVision: A Multi-Agent Framework for Stock Market Prediction
headline_mechanism: FinVision coordinates news-summary, visual technical-analysis, short/medium reflection, and final prediction agents; the last agent emits Buy/Sell/Hold, a 1-10 position size, and an explanation.

source_anchors.claim: The summarizer converts prior-day news into concise factual trading information.
A vision agent interprets a 60-day candlestick and technical-indicator chart.
One reflection agent analyzes recent trade performance and another reviews a 30-day signal chart.
The decision agent synthesizes news, technical analysis, and both reflections into action, 1-10 size, and explanation.

preserved_elements: separate news-summary and technical-analysis agent scores
two distinct short- and medium-horizon reflection scores
one final prediction agent aggregating all four upstream perspectives
rolling feedback from realized earlier outcomes
approximated_elements: earnings, attention, and recent-return characteristics replace unavailable daily news summaries
three-month momentum/volatility characteristics replace 60-day chart images
three- and twelve-month past-return memories replace textual and visual reflection agents
rolling RankIC-based reliability weights replace LangGraph LLM deliberation
continuous consensus confidence replaces sampled action and position-size text
invented_elements: the exact JKP feature bundles for news and chart agents
softmax reliability temperature and action thresholds
common value-weighted long/short decile portfolio adapter
portfolio_adapter: The continuous multi-agent consensus is ranked within the frozen monthly top-1,000 universe and mapped to common value-weighted long/short deciles with 10 bp one-way cost; action and size remain diagnostics.
claim_boundary: This is a researcher-authored FinVision-inspired numerical multi-agent consensus, not the unavailable LangGraph system, news/chart inputs, GPT/o1 responses, action trajectory, position ledger, or native results.
